artifacts.synopsis: Tennessee Valley Presbytery approved without exception Session minutes planning a youth group Super Bowl Party on Sunday; the SJC denied the complaint because the record was insufficient to find Presbytery erred in its constitutional interpretation. A dissent by RE Eggert argued the complaint was judicially out of order because the SJC lacks constitutional authority to review a presbytery's session-records review decisions under BCO 40-2 and 40-3.

artifacts.title: Lewis v. Presbytery of the Mississippi Valley
artifacts.synopsis: The SJC ruled that Anna Lewis's BCO 40-5 report filed directly with the SJC was out of order, holding that the SJC's only responsibility under Chapter 40 arises upon referral from the General Assembly per RAO 16-10.c. Six members dissented, arguing the SJC has historically exercised direct jurisdiction over BCO 40-5 reports and that the majority's interpretation was overly narrow and a departure from settled precedent.

artifacts.synopsis: Northern California Presbytery adopted an abstract resolution declaring six different views on the diaconate permissible for ministers and Sessions; the SJC sustained the complaints and annulled the resolution, holding that no court may issue binding abstract decrees beyond its proper jurisdictional exercise. A concurring opinion analyzed each of the six diaconal views in detail and set out standards (the GUMP/Kniseley framework) for when diaconal assistant practices are constitutionally permissible.
